method.source: frozen M1 difference rasters + common-valid masks
method.threshold_rule: recorded primary threshold of each index (|Δ| ≥ t)
method.geometry: rasterio.features.shapes on the native UTM grid, projected to WGS84 (pyproj); no hand-drawn geometry
method.area_convention: pixel count × pixel area on the projected analysis grid

interpretation.title: ▲ Candidate NDWI increase · Region 01
interpretation.observed_measurement: Mean ΔNDWI +0.218 index units (median +0.204 index units) at the recorded threshold |Δ| ≥ 0.15; 7,481 px = 74.81 ha = 6.56 % of the 114,067-px shared-valid footprint.
interpretation.meaning: A NDWI increase here marks where the later composite reads higher in NDWI. This investigation is PARTIAL: no clean immediate post-event observation exists, and the processed pair is seasonal (April → October), so snow, ice and seasonal spectral evolution dominate the comparison.
explanations: Seasonal snow and ice evolution between the two acquisition windows.
Cloud, shadow and topographic effects at the mask boundary.
Event-related surface change — cannot be established from this seasonal pair.
interpretation.evidence_strength: Shared-valid coverage for this comparison is 100.00 % of the AOI (114,067 px). The region is a connected 7,481-px component at a stated threshold — adjacent pixels are not independent observations, so no significance is claimed. Candidate spectral signal with stated thresholds, not independently verified change.
cannot_conclude: Discharged volume, flood depth, or confirmed event damage from these optical differences.
Any attribution of the mapped difference to the event itself.

source.method: frozen M1 difference rasters + common-valid masks

limitations: Monsoon cloud; terrain shadow; approximate AOI centre.
No volume or dam-failure inference from area alone.
The following indices use 20 m SWIR bands resampled to the 10 m analysis grid and contain no genuine 10 m SWIR detail: ndsi.
Composites are robust within-period summaries of a few observations, not a dense time series; inter-annual change is represented by two period composites only.
Index differences are candidate spectral signals. They are not verified deforestation, wetland loss, construction, glacier damage or any other causal land-cover label.
Cloud, shadow and saturated-pixel exclusion relies on the provider SCL product; terrain shadow is not independently re-derived.
Surface reflectance is the provider L2A product; no independent atmospheric correction is performed.
Areas are planimetric on the documented projected grid; UTM scale distortion at this AOI is small but nonzero.
